# Environment assets

## `sk-skyline.glb`

Swing Kings' authored set dressing (ticket 27): the skyline beyond the
ballpark and the set edge around the stands, replacing the shared box
skyline (`render/env/backdrop.js`, which stays the default for every other
scene) in that one game.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Source | Original — generated by `tools/assets/blender/build-sk-set.py` (bpy, fixed seed, no hand sculpting, no outside reference assets) |
| License | Original work for this project; CC0 |
| Built by | `node tools/assets/blender/run-blender.mjs tools/assets/blender/build-sk-set.py` (Blender 4.2.16 LTS) — writes this file directly; deterministic, see the script header for every piece and the layout numbers it mirrors from `swingKings/world.js` |
| Contents | two flat-shaded static meshes, authored in Swing Kings' world coordinates (added at the origin, no transform), attributes `POSITION`/`NORMAL`/`COLOR_0` only, placeholder materials (the game swaps in house toon materials): **`skyline`** (4,816 tris) — setback towers, a domed arena, a water tower, a crane, two radio masts and two distant light towers over a continuous low-rise band, on an arc 58–76 units behind the stands; vertex colour is a grey value only, the hue comes from the palette at runtime. **`setEdge`** (2,728 tris) — stepped end walls capping both open ends of the stand shell (tunnel mouth, accent stripe), pylons landing both ends of the roof ring, a parapet along the top of the stands, a padded yellow-capped outfield wall, and a concourse apron from the grass edge outwards; vertex colour is the real stadium colour |
| Cost | 2 draw calls in game (one per mesh), no shadow casting; ~7.5k triangles |
